newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: KOF says indicators up but no Swiss revival yet.
newsitem.headline: KOF says indicators up but no Swiss revival yet.

text.p: One of Switzerland's top three economic institutes on Wednesday said its economic barometer rose in October, but not enough to signal a return to growth from this year's economic constriction.
The Centre for Research of Economic Activity (KOF) said the KOF/ETH index of early indicators was down overall in the third quarter period July through September based on revised data.
It said the barometer rose a preliminary 0.2 percent in October from September and 0.9 percent from a year earlier.
That compared with revised month-on-month declines of 0.2 percent in September and 0.1 percent each in August and July.

"Based on the revised data, the adjusted KOF/ETH barometer for the third quarter has once again fallen more strongly below longer-term average levels and the slight improvement in October cannot yet be interpreted as a reversal," KOF said.

"Based on the development of the barometer so far in the second half of this year, a solid economic improvement cannot be expected in the first months of next year," said a statement from the institute, part of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH).
KOF last month said the preliminary September barometer rose 0.1 percent from August and 1.1 percent from a year before.
The latest statement said that revised September data had forced large downward corrections in the indicators for machinery industry orders and jobn vacancies.
"The only continued expansion was shown by the monetary indicator (real money supply)," KOF addded.
Other indices that make up the barometer include an early construction indicator and a share index.
